selection: Dispatch inert authored selection data by its explicit language and exact schema/profile. Python selects its registered native whole-project planner; TypeScript retains its existing planner. No planner failure selects another language or legacy path. Python does not accept a TypeScript numeric realization option.
entrypoints: Existing explicit source/snapshot build, qualified node and project instantiation APIs and build/instantiate/instantiate-project/verify CLI commands use the same checked Python plan and exact views. Snapshot and node planning never reload source; source planning retains currentness checking. Omitted compilation selection preserves all legacy calls and defaults.
layout: For Python only, application-layout/v1 prefixes native artifact and internal module target paths with domain/python/src/. Keep original Python source bytes, relative imports, package initializers and native identifiers unchanged. The receipt remains evidence/project-build.json. Node-scoped application layout is unsupported. TypeScript keeps its prior extension and domain/typescript/src/ prefix.
identity: Python output, build and instantiation wrappers and explicit application views additionally bind this language extension digest. The registered Python whole-project plan is also its resolved plan identity; it is not a fabricated TypeScript resolved artifact plan. Preserve all predecessor compiler source bytes and contract identities.
effects: Only explicit local publication materializes output through the existing atomic no-replace publisher. Reject existing targets, forged plans, conflicting options and unsupported inputs before output effects. Planning does not execute providers or native code.
verification: The shared verify command is exact artifact-currentness only, including receipt and complete path inventory. Native compilation, semantic observation and formal verification remain explicitly not-performed in these receipts. Separate native tests qualify the actual published Python bytes and domain behavior.
remaining: Python cross-project composition adapters and stronger verify-project integration remain required before R10 closure. Unsupported paths reject explicitly; this extension grants no release, admission, default cutover or external effect.
